'''Hibita Shrine''' (ひびたじんじゃ) is an old shrine of the former {{ill|Sagami Province|ckb|پارێزگای ساگامی|cs|Provincie Sagami|de|Provinz Sagami|es|Provincia de Sagami|fa|ولایت ساگامی|fr|Province de Sagami|gl|Provincia de Sagami|id|Provinsi Sagami|it|Sagami (provincia)|ja|相模国|ko|사가미국|lt|Sagamio žemė|nl|Sagami (provincie)|pt|Província de Sagami|ru|Сагами (провинция)|simple|Sagami Province|sk|Sagami (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сагами|tr|Sagami (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Саґамі|zh|相模國|zh_min_nan|Sagami-kok|zh_yue|相模國|qid=Q1053732}} in Sannomiya, {{ill|Isehara, Kanagawa|ar|إسيهارا (كاناغاوا)|azb|ایسه‌هارا، کاناقاوا|be|Ісехара|ca|Isehara|ce|Исехара|ceb|Isehara|de|Isehara|eo|Isehara|es|Isehara|et|Isehara|fa|ایسه‌هارا، کاناگاوا|fi|Isehara|fr|Isehara|gl|Isehara|it|Isehara|ja|伊勢原市|ko|이세하라시|mg|Isehara|mzn|ایسه‌هارا، کاناگاوا|nl|Isehara|no|Isehara|pl|Isehara|pt|Isehara|ro|Isehara|ru|Исехара|sh|Isehara|sr|Исехара|sv|Isehara|tg|Исеҳара|th|อิเซฮาระ|tl|Isehara, Kanagawa|tr|Isehara|tt|Исехара|uk|Ісехара|ur|اسیہارا، کاناگاوا|uz|Isehara (Kanagawa)|vi|Isehara, Kanagawa|war|Isehara, Kanagawa|zh|伊勢原市|zh_classical|伊勢原市|zh_min_nan|Isehara-chhī|zh_yue|伊勢原|qid=Q734520}}, {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture|Q127513|qid=Q127513}}. Its former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine rank}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}, and today it is a {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture Shrine Office Designated Shrine|Q11588941|qid=Q11588941|lt=heihaku-messenger visiting shrine}} under the Kanagawa {{ill|Jinjachō|Q11590703|qid=Q11590703}}. In older times it was also called '''Kanmuri Daimyōjin'''.

It is considered to be '''Hibita Shrine''' listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}' of {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) (one of the 13 Engishiki shrines of Sagami Province, minor shrine), but as noted {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=below}}, there are also {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=competing claims}}. It is one of the five Sagami shrines participating in the old-Sagami traditional {{ill|Festival|Q132241|qid=Q132241|lt=rite}}, the {{ill|Kokufu-sai|Q11420919|qid=Q11420919|lt=Kōno-machi}}, held every {{ill|May 5|Q2550|qid=Q2550}} at Kamisoroi-yama in Kokufu-Hongō, {{ill|Ōiso|Q385023|qid=Q385023}}, and corresponds to the province’s {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Sannomiya}}. The place name “Sannomiya” derives from this shrine, and it has long also been called “'''Sannomiya-sama'''.”

=== Enshrined deities ===
Principal deities
* Toyokumunu-no-Mikoto ({{ill|Toyokumono-no-Mikoto|es|Toyo-kumo-no-no-kami|ja|トヨクモノ|ru|Тоё-кумоно-но ками|uk|Тойо кумоно но камі|zh|豐斟渟尊|qid=Q4387158|lt=Toyokuninushi-no-Mikoto}})
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ame no Akaru Tama no Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Wakahiru-me|ja|稚日女尊|zh|稚日女尊|qid=Q11596349|lt=Wakahirume-no-Mikoto}}
* {{ill|Yamato Takeru|lt=Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258}}

{{ill|Andrea Di Stefano|Q1107120|qid=Q1107120}} (accompanying hall deities)
* Ōsakatoke-no-Kami ({{ill|Ōyamatsumi|lt=Ōyamatsumi|Q386563|qid=Q386563|qid=Q386563|lt=Ōyamatsumi-no-Kami}})
* Kosakatoke-no-Kami ({{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime}})

The above are regarded as the current deities, but according to 'Nihon no Kamigami: Shrines and Sacred Sites 11 Kantō'<ref name="kamigami">Edited by Ken'ichi Tanigawa, 'Nihon no Kamigami: Shrines and Sacred Sites 11 Kantō' (Hakusuisha, Dec. 1984).</ref>, there were once four theories. Three are generally similar to the current deities, but notable is the inscription on the temple bell at the shrine (now lost; for the reason see “{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=History}}” below) described in '{{ill|Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudoki-kō|Q11503942|qid=Q11503942}} Vol. 50'<ref name="hudokikou">Included in Itojin Ashida (ed.), 'Dai Nihon Chishi Taikei 17: Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudokikō Vol. 3' (Yūzankaku, Sept. 1962).</ref>, saying the spirit of Someya Tarō-dayū Tokitada, Kamakura military commander in the {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyō era}}, was enshrined<ref group="注">According to 'Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudokikō Vol. 50,' this is said to be the father of {{ill|Rōben|Q720819|qid=Q720819}}, founder of Mount Ōyama in the 'Ōyama Engi.'</ref>. However, that same book states that this is hard to trust because it differs greatly from current shrine tradition.

=== History ===
=== Origin ===
According to 'Hibita Denki' written in {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} 5 ({{ill|1834|Q7591|qid=Q7591}})<ref name="shaden">Included in Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee (ed.), 'Shintō Taikei: Shrine Section 16 Suruga, Izu, Kai, Sagami' (Shintō Taikei Editorial Committee, Mar. 1980).</ref>, the shrine was established during {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ar|الإمبراطور جينمو|arz|الامبراطور جينمو|as|জিম্মু|az|Cimmu|bcl|Emperador Jimmu|be|Імператар Дзіму|ca|Jinmu|cdo|Sìng-ū Tiĕng-huòng|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر جینمو|cs|Džimmu|de|Jimmu|el|Αυτοκράτορας Τζίμου|eo|Imperiestro Jinmu|es|Jinmu Tennō|et|Jimmu|eu|Jimmu enperadorea|fa|امپراتور جینمو|fi|Jinmu|fr|Jinmu|hak|Sṳ̀n-vú Thiên-fòng|he|ג'ימו, קיסר יפן|hi|सम्राट जिममु|hr|Jinmu|hu|Dzsinmu japán császár|id|Jimmu|it|Jinmu|ja|神武天皇|jv|Jimmu Tenno|ka|ძიმუ|ko|진무 천황|kw|Emperour Jimmu|la|Jimmu|lt|Imperatorius Džinmu|lv|Džimmu|mn|Эзэн Хаан Жиммү|mr|जिम्मू|ms|Maharaja Jimmu|my|ဂျင်းမူ ဧကရာဇ်|nl|Jimmu|no|Jimmu|pl|Jimmu|pt|Jimmu|ru|Император Дзимму|sh|Car Jimmu|simple|Emperor Jimmu|sl|Cesar Džinmu|sr|Џинму|sv|Jimmu|th|จักรพรรดิจิมมุ|tl|Emperador Jimmu|tr|Jimmu|uk|Імператор Дзімму|uz|Jimmu|vi|Thiên hoàng Jimmu|war|Emperador Jimmu|wuu|神武天皇|zh|神武天皇|zh_classical|神武天皇|zh_min_nan|Sîn-bú Thian-hông|zh_yue|神武天皇|qid=Q200188}}’s pacification of the realm to protect the people. According to 'Hibita Shrine Worship Guide'<ref group="注" name="shiori">'Hibita Shrine Worship Guide' is a pamphlet distributed at the shrine.</ref>, this was in Jimmu 6 ({{ill|655 BC|Q720071|qid=Q720071}}): people selected this place, where rituals had long been performed, as best, and enshrined Toyokuninushi-no-Mikoto as the spirit of Japan with {{ill|Mount Ōyama (Kanagawa)|Q386518|qid=Q386518|lt=Mount Ōyama}} as the {{ill|Sacred mountains|ar|جبال مقدسة|ca|Muntanyes sagrades|de|Heiliger Berg|es|Montaña sagrada|fa|کوه‌های مقدس|fi|Pyhä vuori|fr|Montagne sacrée|id|Gunung keramat|ja|神体山|lt|Alkakalnis|lv|Svētie kalni|pl|Święte góry|ru|Священная гора|sq|Malet e shenjta|uk|Священна гора|vi|Núi thiêng|qid=Q1595289}}.

Meanwhile, from ruins and artifacts excavated in and near the precincts, a {{ill|standing stone|Q11598071|qid=Q11598071|lt=standing stone}} within a mid-{{ill|Jōmon period|Q52824|qid=Q52824}} {{ill|Stone circle|Q1935728|qid=Q1935728}} is estimated to be a ritual site. The shrine side estimates that the origin of this shrine may go back to primal Jōmon {{ill|Mountain worship|Q93697439|qid=Q93697439}} over 10,000 years ago, potentially making it one of eastern Japan’s oldest shrines. This shrine stands on the southeastern foot of Mount Ōyama; 'Nihon no Kamigami: 11 Kantō'<ref name="kamigami" /> also considers that it was likely originally a shrine for distant worship of Mount Ōyama.

=== Ancient period ===
According to 'Hibita Denki'<ref name="shaden" />, in {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} 7 ({{ill|91 BC|Q40968|qid=Q40968}}), shrine lands and {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711|lt=kannbe households}} were granted; in the 8th month of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|ar|الإمبراطور سوينين|arz|الامبراطور سوينين|azb|سوینین (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Suinin|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر سوینین|cs|Suinin|de|Suinin|eo|Suinin|es|Suinin Tennō|fa|امپراتور سوینین|fi|Suinin|fr|Suinin|hr|Suinin|id|Kaisar Suinin|it|Suinin|ja|垂仁天皇|ka|სუინინი|ko|스이닌 천황|lt|Imperatorius Suininas|mn|Эзэн Хаан Сүйнин|nl|Suinin|pl|Suinin|pt|Suinin|ru|Император Суйнин|sh|Car Suinin|simple|Emperor Suinin|sl|Cesar Sujnin|sr|Суинин|sv|Suinin|th|จักรพรรดิซูอินิง|tl|Emperador Suinin|tr|Suinin (imparator)|uk|Імператор Суйнін|uz|Imperator Suinin|vi|Thiên hoàng Suinin|yo|Emperor Suinin|zh|垂仁天皇|zh_min_nan|Suinin Thian-hông|zh_yue|垂仁天皇|qid=Q314850}} 27 ({{ill|3 BC|Q39821|qid=Q39821}}), by imperial order, the Jingikan offered bows and arrows. According to 'Hibita Shrine Worship Guide'<ref group="注" name="shiori" />, in {{ill|Taika (era)|Q1077930|qid=Q1077930}} 1 ({{ill|645|Q31040|qid=Q31040}}), two deities, Ōsakatoke and Kosakatoke, were enshrined together, and at that time a {{ill|Sue pottery|Q7634351|qid=Q7634351}} vessel called “Uzuramika”<ref group="注">Read "uzuramika." It leaves the main sanctuary only for the Sake Festival ritual in late November each year. It is designated an Important Cultural Property of Kanagawa Prefecture.</ref> was deposited. Also according to the guide<ref group="注" name="shiori" />, in {{ill|Empress Jitō|Q232026|qid=Q232026}} 6 ({{ill|692|Q23477|qid=Q23477}}), provincial governor Fuse no Ason Shikofuchi repaired the shrine buildings and dedicated a pair of {{ill|Komainu|Q20155846|qid=Q20155846}}<ref group="注">This wooden pair of komainu is designated an Important Cultural Property of Kanagawa Prefecture.</ref>. In {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 15 ({{ill|743|Q23604|qid=Q23604}}), Ki no Ason Masumaro, a descendant of {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}}, became first chief priest, and {{ill|Emperor Shōmu|Q349263|qid=Q349263}} granted {{ill|Shōen|Q1887569|qid=Q1887569|lt=estate land}}. According to the guide<ref group="注" name="shiori" />, in {{ill|Tenchō|Q1373138|qid=Q1373138}} 9 ({{ill|832|Q23900|qid=Q23900}}), as imperial envoy, provincial governor Tachibana no Ason Minetsugu bestowed by order of {{ill|Emperor Junna|Q374136|qid=Q374136}} the divine title “'''Kanmuri Daimyōjin'''” of the {{ill|Sagami Province|ckb|پارێزگای ساگامی|cs|Provincie Sagami|de|Provinz Sagami|es|Provincia de Sagami|fa|ولایت ساگامی|fr|Province de Sagami|gl|Provincia de Sagami|id|Provinsi Sagami|it|Sagami (provincia)|ja|相模国|ko|사가미국|lt|Sagamio žemė|nl|Sagami (provincie)|pt|Província de Sagami|ru|Сагами (провинция)|simple|Sagami Province|sk|Sagami (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сагами|tr|Sagami (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Саґамі|zh|相模國|zh_min_nan|Sagami-kok|zh_yue|相模國|qid=Q1053732}} {{ill|Sōja shrine|Q1107129|qid=Q1107129}}<ref group="注">A similar tradition appears in the 'National Shrine Directory Vol. 1' (July 1977), though some dates differ.</ref>.

The '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}' completed in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} 5 ({{ill|927|ab|927|af|927|am|927 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|927|ar|927|ary|927|ast|927|avk|927|az|927|azb|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|bar|927|bcl|927|be|927|be_x_old|927|bg|927|bn|৯২৭|bpy|মারি ৯২৭|br|927|bs|927.|ca|927|cdo|927 nièng|ceb|927|ckb|٩٢٧|crh|927|cs|927|csb|927|cv|927|cy|927|da|927|de|927|el|927|eml|927|eo|927|es|927|et|927|eu|927|fa|۹۲۷ (میلادی)|fi|927|fo|927|fr|927|fy|927|ga|927|gan|927年|gd|927|gl|927|he|927|hi|927|hr|927.|ht|927 (almanak jilyen)|hu|927|hy|927|id|927|ilo|927|io|927|is|927|it|927|ja|927年|jv|927|ka|927|kaa|927|kk|927 жыл|ko|927년|la|927|lb|927|lij|927|lmo|927|lt|927 m.|lv|927. gads|map_bms|927|mdf|927|mg|927|mhr|927|mi|927|mk|927|mr|इ.स. ९२७|mrj|927 и|ms|927|mzn|۹۲۷|nah|927|nap|927|nds|927|new|सन् ९२७|nl|927|nn|927|no|927|nrm|927|nso|927|oc|927|or|୯୨୭|os|927-æм аз|pl|927|pnb|927|pt|927|qu|927|ro|927|ru|927 год|rue|927|sa|९२७|scn|927|sd|927ع|se|927|sh|927.|shn|927|si|927|sk|927|smn|927|sq|927|sr|927|su|927|sv|927|sw|927|tg|Соли 927|th|พ.ศ. 1470|tk|927|tl|927|tly|927|tr|927|tt|927 ел|uk|927|ur|927ء|uz|927|vec|927|vi|927|war|927|wuu|927年|xmf|927|zh|927年|zh_min_nan|927 nî|zh_yue|927年|qid=Q30470}}) lists “Hibita Shrine” as one of four minor shrines in {{ill|Ōsumi district|Q11432367|qid=Q11432367}}, Sagami Province. But according to 'Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudokikō Vol. 50'<ref name="hudokikou" />, besides this shrine, {{ill|Hibita Shrine (Q11547458)|Q11547458|qid=Q11547458|lt=Koyasu Myōjin Shrine}} in Kamikasuya village (now Kamikasuya, Isehara) is also said to have been the Shikinaisha “Hibita Shrine.” The same book introduces a story told by this shrine’s chief priest: a plaque inscribed “Hibita Shrine” was lent to the Koyasu shrine priest and never returned, and Koyasu shrine then displayed it and claimed Shikinaisha status. It then says there is no evidence for this story, and since there is no proof either this shrine or Koyasu shrine is Engishiki “Hibita Shrine,” it is difficult to judge which one is correct. In 'Nihon no Kamigami: 11 Kantō'<ref name="kamigami" />, considering that this site overlooks an ancient official road and is a strong candidate location for the second-phase {{ill|Kokufu|Q1629088|qid=Q1629088}} of Sagami, that shrine tradition says it was the sōsha when the provincial capital was there, and judging from red-seal documents issued to both shrines in the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, this shrine is considered likely the Engishiki “Hibita Shrine.”

=== Medieval period ===
In {{ill|Genryaku|Q1194250|qid=Q1194250}} 1 ({{ill|1184|Q19728|qid=Q19728}}), {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}} carried out major reconstruction, and in {{ill|Bunji (era)|Q1194415|qid=Q1194415}} 1 ({{ill|1185|Q19729|qid=Q19729}}), submitted a prayer document for peace under heaven. Also, the entry for August 9, {{ill|Kenkyū|Q1193933|qid=Q1193933}} 3 ({{ill|1192|Q19739|qid=Q19739}}), in the '{{ill|Azuma Kagami|Q1042324|qid=Q1042324}}' states Yoritomo prayed at “Sannomiya Kanmuri Daimyōjin” for safe childbirth of {{ill|Hōjō Masako|Q463961|qid=Q463961}}, and dedicated a {{ill|Shinme|Q11591047|qid=Q11591047}}.

=== Early modern period ===
According to 'Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudokikō Vol. 50'<ref name="hudokikou" />, around the {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841|lt=Meiō era}} ({{ill|1492|Q6679|qid=Q6679}}–{{ill|1501|Q6131|qid=Q6131}}), war fire caused loss of shrine lands; shrine officials and affiliated monks dispersed and the shrine greatly declined. The name of Kando village<ref group="注">Present-day Kando, Isehara.</ref> is said to preserve the old name from when it was a sealed household area. The same source says that in early {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058|lt=Tenshō}} ({{ill|1573|Q6678|qid=Q6678}}–{{ill|1593|Q6772|qid=Q6772}}), the shrine site was moved from Racchi-men<ref group="注">Near present Eikō Jogakuen Junior College of Horticulture in Sannomiya, Isehara.</ref> to its current location, and the deity transferred to a small shrine there.

In the 11th month of Tenshō 19 ({{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}}), a vermilion-seal document from {{ill|Tokugawa Ieyasu|Q171977|qid=Q171977}} granted 10 {{ill|Koku|Q855048|qid=Q855048}} of shrine land. 'Shinpen Sagami no Kuni Fudokikō Vol. 50'<ref name="hudokikou" /> says this finally enabled the shrine’s recovery. Thereafter it received donations from successive shoguns into the {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} period.

=== Modern and contemporary period ===
In Meiji 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it was designated {{ill|Q712534|lt=Gōsha}} and became general tutelary shrine of 16 villages. In Meiji 41 ({{ill|1908|Q2056|qid=Q2056}}), it was designated a shrine for official offerings of sacred food and cloth. It is now a {{ill|Kanagawa Prefecture Shrine Office Designated Shrine|Q11588941|qid=Q11588941|lt=heihaku-messenger visiting shrine}} under Kanagawa Shrine Office.

The inscribed temple bell said to have enshrined Someya Tarō-dayū Tokitada was lost during {{ill|Pacific War|Q184425|qid=Q184425}} wartime metal requisition. The current bell was made in {{ill|1950|Q18597|qid=Q18597}} (Shōwa 25).

In {{ill|1953|Q18585|qid=Q18585}} (Shōwa 28), the Sannomiya Local Museum was attached by former {{ill|Gūji|Q11453500|qid=Q11453500}} Nagai Sanji.
